17	# LaTeX 论文写作全流程
18	
19	ML/AI 顶会论文从草稿到投稿的完整指南。整合 Orchestra Research、VibeSkills、claim2evidence 三方最佳实践。
20	
21	---
22	
23	## 1. 工作模式
24	
25	开始前选择模式：
26	
27	| 模式 | 说明 | 适用 |
28	|------|------|------|
29	| **Build** | 从实验笔记/结果/代码生成论文 | 新稿 |
30	| **Improve** | 改写已有章节，强化论证 | 修改稿 |
31	| **Audit** | 输出风险列表 + 缺失证据 + 修复建议 | 投前检查 |
32	
33	---
34	
35	## 2. Claim-Evidence 方法论
36	
37	**核心原则：论文是一个有中心贡献的故事，不是实验的堆砌。**
38	
39	### 2.1 一句话贡献
40	
41	在写任何内容之前，必须能用一句话说清贡献。如果不能，说明还没准备好写论文。
42	
43	### 2.2 Claim-Evidence Map
44	
45	为每个 contribution 建立 claim→evidence 映射表：
46	
47	| Contribution | Claim | Evidence | Table/Figure |
48	|-------------|-------|----------|-------------|
49	| C1: 方法 X 在 Y 上 SOTA | 比所有 baseline 高 ≥2% | 5-seed 平均，p<0.05 | Table 1 |
50	| C2: 消融证明 Z 是关键 | 去掉 Z 后掉 >5% | 消融实验 | Table 2 |
51	| C3: 计算效率 | 比 baseline 快 3× | FLOPs + wall-clock | Figure 3 |
52	
53	**没有直接证据支撑的 claim 必须删除或降级为 discussion。**
54	
55	### 2.3 章节起草顺序
56	
57	```
58	1. Introduction + Experiments（先确定 claim 和 evidence）
59	2. Method（评估问题稳定后再写细节）
60	3. Related Work
61	4. Abstract + Title（核心 claim 定型后最后写）
62	```
63	
64	### 2.4 Quality Gates
65	
66	投稿前必须通过：
67	- [ ] 前两段出现显式 novelty 声明
68	- [ ] 每个 contribution 有可验证的 evidence
69	- [ ] Abstract / Intro / Conclusion 的 claim 一致
70	- [ ] Limitations 真实且技术性诚实
71	- [ ] 审稿人两分钟内能识别 delta
72	
73	---
74	
75	## 3. 引用防幻觉（CRITICAL）
76	
77	**AI 生成引用有 ~40% 错误率。绝对禁止凭记忆写 BibTeX。**
78	
79	### 3.1 黄金法则
80	
81	```
82	IF 无法程序化获取引用:
83	    → 标记 [CITATION NEEDED] 或 \cite{PLACEHOLDER_verify}
84	    → 明确告知用户
85	    → 绝不编造看似合理的引用
86	```
87	
88	### 3.2 五步验证流程
89	
90	```
91	1. SEARCH  → Semantic Scholar API 搜索关键词
92	2. VERIFY  → 至少 2 个来源确认论文存在（S2 + arXiv/CrossRef）
93	3. RETRIEVE → 通过 DOI 获取 BibTeX（程序化，非记忆）
94	4. CHECK   → 确认你引用的 claim 确实出自该论文
95	5. ADD     → 加入 .bib 文件
96	```
97	
98	### 3.3 API 速查
99	
100	| API | 用途 | 限制 |
101	|-----|------|------|
102	| **Semantic Scholar** | ML/AI 论文搜索 | 1 RPS (免费) |
103	| **CrossRef** | DOI → BibTeX | 需 mailto 头 |
104	| **arXiv** | 预印本搜索 | 3s 间隔 |
105	
106	```python
107	# DOI → BibTeX（最可靠的方式）
108	import requests
109	def doi_to_bibtex(doi: str) -> str:
110	    r = requests.get(f"https://doi.org/{doi}",
111	                     headers={"Accept": "application/x-bibtex"})
112	    r.raise_for_status()
113	    return r.text
114	
115	# Semantic Scholar 搜索
116	from semanticscholar import SemanticScholar
117	sch = SemanticScholar()
118	results = sch.search_paper("attention mechanism transformers", limit=5)
119	for p in results:
120	    print(f"{p.title} | DOI: {p.externalIds.get('DOI', 'N/A')}")
121	```
122	
123	### 3.4 引用处理规则
124	
125	| 情况 | 处理 |
126	|------|------|
127	| 找到论文 + DOI + BibTeX | 直接用 |
128	| 找到论文，无 DOI | 用 arXiv BibTeX |
129	| 论文存在但无法获取 BibTeX | 标记 placeholder，告知用户 |
130	| 不确定论文是否存在 | 标记 `[CITATION NEEDED]`，告知用户 |
131	| "我觉得有篇关于 X 的论文" | **绝不引用** — 先搜索或标记 |
132	
133	---
134	
135	## 4. 顶会模板速查
136	
137	### 4.1 ML/AI 会议
138	
139	| 会议 | 页数限制 | 主文件 | 样式文件 | 必须项 |
140	|------|---------|--------|---------|--------|
141	| **NeurIPS** | 9 页 | `main.tex` | `neurips.sty` | Paper Checklist |
142	| **ICML** | 8 页 (+1 camera-ready) | `example_paper.tex` | `icml2026.sty` | Broader Impact |
143	| **ICLR** | 9 页 (+1) | `iclr_conference.tex` | `iclr_conference.sty` | LLM 使用声明 |
144	| **ACL/EMNLP** | 8 页 (long) | `acl_latex.tex` | `acl.sty` | Limitations 必须 |
145	| **AAAI** | 7 页 (+1) | `aaai_template.tex` | `aaai.sty` | 严格样式 |
146	| **COLM** | 9 页 (+1) | `colm_conference.tex` | `colm_conference.sty` | 语言模型聚焦 |
147	
148	### 4.2 系统会议
149	
150	| 会议 | 页数限制 | 模板类型 | 关键要求 |
151	|------|---------|---------|---------|
152	| **OSDI** | 12 页 (+2) | USENIX `usenix.sty` | Research / Operational 双 track |
153	| **NSDI** | 12 页 | USENIX | Introduction 预筛 |
154	| **ASPLOS** | 12 页 | ACM `acmart.cls (sigplan)` | 前 2 页快速评审 |
155	| **SOSP** | 12 页 | ACM `acmart.cls (sigplan)` | 可选 Artifact Evaluation |
156	
157	### 4.3 模板使用原则
158	
159	```bash
160	# 1. 复制整个模板目录（不要只拷 .tex）
161	cp -r templates/neurips2025/ ~/papers/my-paper/
162	
163	# 2. 先编译未修改的模板，确认能跑通
164	latexmk -pdf main.tex
165	
166	# 3. 逐章替换内容，频繁编译
167	```
168	
169	**禁止事项：**
170	- 不要修改 `.sty` 文件
171	- 不要在会议模板间复制 `\usepackage` 行
172	- 不要只复制 `.tex` 而不带 `.sty/.bst`
173	
174	---
175	
176	## 5. 写作规范
177	
178	### 5.1 时间分配（Neel Nanda）
179	
180	花**大致相等**的时间在：
181	1. Abstract
182	2. Introduction
183	3. 图表
184	4. **其余所有内容加起来**
185	
186	审稿人读论文的顺序：标题 → 摘要 → 引言 → 图表 → 也许正文。
187	
188	### 5.2 Abstract 五句法（Sebastian Farquhar）
189	
190	```
191	1. 你做了什么（"We introduce/prove/demonstrate..."）
192	2. 为什么这很难且重要
193	3. 怎么做的（含专业关键词以便检索）
194	4. 有什么证据
195	5. 最惊人的数字/结果
196	```
197	
198	删除一切泛泛的开头：~~"Large language models have achieved remarkable success..."~~
199	
200	### 5.3 句子级清晰度（Gopen & Swan）
201	
202	| 原则 | 规则 |
203	|------|------|
204	| 主谓紧邻 | 不要在主语和动词之间插入长从句 |
205	| 重点在句尾 | 把关键数字/结论放在句末 |
206	| 旧信息在前 | 先放读者已知的内容，再引入新概念 |
207	| 动词表达动作 | "We analyzed" 而非 "We performed an analysis" |
208	
209	### 5.4 常见修改
210	
211	| 问题 | 修复 |
212	|------|------|
213	| Abstract 太泛 | 删第一句（如果它能放在任何 ML 论文前面） |
214	| Introduction 超 1.5 页 | 背景挪到 Related Work |
215	| 实验没有显式 claim | 每个实验前加 "This tests whether..." |
216	| 缺统计显著性 | 加 error bars + 运行次数 + 计算方法 |
217	
218	---
219	
220	## 6. 投稿工程链
221	
222	### 6.1 构建
223	
224	```bash
225	# 推荐：latexmk 一键构建
226	latexmk -pdf -interaction=nonstopmode -halt-on-error main.tex
227	
228	# 手动：需要多次编译
229	pdflatex main.tex && bibtex main && pdflatex main.tex && pdflatex main.tex
230	```
231	
232	### 6.2 Lint + 格式化
233	
234	```bash
235	# Lint: 检查常见 LaTeX 问题
236	chktex main.tex
237	
238	# 格式化: 减少 diff 噪声
239	latexindent -w main.tex
240	```
241	
242	### 6.3 图表格式
243	
244	| 类型 | 格式 | 说明 |
245	|------|------|------|
246	| 矢量图（plot、diagram） | PDF | matplotlib: `plt.savefig('fig.pdf')` |
247	| 照片/heatmap | PNG 600dpi 或 TIFF | 栅格图 |
248	| 表格 | `booktabs` 包 | `\toprule/\midrule/\bottomrule` |
249	
250	```latex
251	\usepackage{booktabs}
252	\begin{tabular}{lcc}
253	\toprule
254	Method & Accuracy $\uparrow$ & Latency $\downarrow$ \\
255	\midrule
256	Baseline & 85.2 & 45ms \\
257	\textbf{Ours} & \textbf{92.1} & 38ms \\
258	\bottomrule
259	\end{tabular}
260	```
261	
262	**图表规范：**
263	- 用色盲友好色板（Okabe-Ito 或 Paul Tol）
264	- 图内不放标题（用 caption）
265	- Caption 独立可理解（不依赖正文）
266	- 最佳值加粗，标注方向符号（↑ 越高越好，↓ 越低越好）
267	
268	### 6.4 投稿打包
269	
270	```bash
271	# 清理辅助文件
272	latexmk -c
273	
274	# 打包投稿
275	zip -r submission.zip main.tex *.sty *.bst *.bib figures/ --exclude='*.aux' --exclude='*.log'
276	```
277	
278	### 6.5 常见失败点
279	
280	| 问题 | 解决 |
281	|------|------|
282	| 图片格式混用导致编译失败 | 统一用 PDF |
283	| 字体未嵌入 | `pdffonts output.pdf` 检查 |
284	| Overfull box 过多 | 关键位置手动调行 |
285	| 引用缺字段 | 检查 DOI/年份/期刊名 |
286	| 超页数 | 用 `\vspace{-Xpt}` 微调，或精简内容 |
287	
288	---
289	
290	## 7. 会议转投
291	
292	当论文被拒或转投其他会议时：
293	
294	### 7.1 ML/AI 会议间转换
295	
296	| 转换 | 页数变化 | 关键调整 |
297	|------|---------|---------|
298	| NeurIPS → ICML | 9→8 | 删 1 页，加 Broader Impact |
299	| ICML → ICLR | 8→9 | 可扩展实验 + LLM 声明 |
300	| NeurIPS → ACL | 9→8 | 按 NLP 惯例重组 + Limitations |
301	| ICLR → AAAI | 9→7 | 大幅精简，严格样式 |
302	
303	### 7.2 转投原则
304	
305	1. **永远用目标模板重新开始** — 复制目标模板，迁移内容，不要合并 preamble
306	2. **只迁移正文内容** — 不复制 `\usepackage`、header/footer 命令
307	3. **根据审稿意见改进** — 但不要在新稿中提及旧投稿（双盲）
308	4. **检查目标会议特殊要求** — checklist、ethics statement、LLM 声明等
309	
310	---
311	
312	## 8. 投前清单
313	
314	### 通用清单
315	
316	- [ ] Abstract/Intro/Conclusion 的 claim 一致
317	- [ ] 每个 contribution 有对应 evidence
318	- [ ] 所有引用已程序化验证（无幻觉引用）
319	- [ ] Error bars + 运行次数 + 统计方法
320	- [ ] Limitations 章节存在且诚实
321	- [ ] 匿名化（双盲审稿）
322	- [ ] 符合页数限制
323	- [ ] 所有图表有自包含 caption
324	- [ ] `.bib` 中无缺失字段
325	- [ ] PDF 编译无 warning
326	
327	### 会议特定
328	
329	| 会议 | 额外要求 |
330	|------|---------|
331	| NeurIPS | 16 项 Paper Checklist（附录，不计页数） |
332	| ICML | Broader Impact Statement |
333	| ICLR | LLM 使用声明 |
334	| ACL/EMNLP | Limitations 章节（必须），Ethics Statement |
335	| AAAI | 严格样式文件合规 |
336	
337	---
338	
339	## 参考资源
340	
341	**写作方法论：**
342	- [Neel Nanda: How to Write ML Papers](https://www.alignmentforum.org/posts/eJGptPbbFPZGLpjsp/) — What/Why/So What 框架
343	- [Farquhar: How to Write ML Papers](https://sebastianfarquhar.com/on-research/2024/11/04/how_to_write_ml_papers/) — 五句法 Abstract
344	- [Gopen & Swan: Science of Scientific Writing](https://cseweb.ucsd.edu/~swanson/papers/science-of-writing.pdf) — 读者预期 7 原则
345	- [Lipton: Heuristics for Scientific Writing](https://www.approximatelycorrect.com/2018/01/29/heuristics-technical-scientific-writing-machine-learning-perspective/) — 用词
346	- [Perez: Easy Paper Writing Tips](https://ethanperez.net/easy-paper-writing-tips/) — 微观清晰度
347	
348	**API：**
349	- [Semantic Scholar](https://api.semanticscholar.org/api-docs/) | [CrossRef](https://www.crossref.org/documentation/) | [arXiv](https://info.arxiv.org/help/api/)
350	
351	**会议官方：**
352	- [NeurIPS](https://neurips.cc/) | [ICML](https://icml.cc/) | [ICLR](https://iclr.cc/) | [ACL](https://www.aclweb.org/) | [AAAI](https://aaai.org/) | [EMNLP](https://2025.emnlp.org/)

# LaTeX 论文写作全流程

ML/AI 顶会论文从草稿到投稿的完整指南。整合 Orchestra Research、VibeSkills、claim2evidence 三方最佳实践。

---

## 1. 工作模式

开始前选择模式：

| 模式 | 说明 | 适用 |
|------|------|------|
| **Build** | 从实验笔记/结果/代码生成论文 | 新稿 |
| **Improve** | 改写已有章节，强化论证 | 修改稿 |
| **Audit** | 输出风险列表 + 缺失证据 + 修复建议 | 投前检查 |

---

## 2. Claim-Evidence 方法论

**核心原则：论文是一个有中心贡献的故事，不是实验的堆砌。**

### 2.1 一句话贡献

在写任何内容之前，必须能用一句话说清贡献。如果不能，说明还没准备好写论文。

### 2.2 Claim-Evidence Map

为每个 contribution 建立 claim→evidence 映射表：

| Contribution | Claim | Evidence | Table/Figure |
|-------------|-------|----------|-------------|
| C1: 方法 X 在 Y 上 SOTA | 比所有 baseline 高 ≥2% | 5-seed 平均，p<0.05 | Table 1 |
| C2: 消融证明 Z 是关键 | 去掉 Z 后掉 >5% | 消融实验 | Table 2 |
| C3: 计算效率 | 比 baseline 快 3× | FLOPs + wall-clock | Figure 3 |

**没有直接证据支撑的 claim 必须删除或降级为 discussion。**

### 2.3 章节起草顺序

```
1. Introduction + Experiments（先确定 claim 和 evidence）
2. Method（评估问题稳定后再写细节）
3. Related Work
4. Abstract + Title（核心 claim 定型后最后写）
```

### 2.4 Quality Gates

投稿前必须通过：
- [ ] 前两段出现显式 novelty 声明
- [ ] 每个 contribution 有可验证的 evidence
- [ ] Abstract / Intro / Conclusion 的 claim 一致
- [ ] Limitations 真实且技术性诚实
- [ ] 审稿人两分钟内能识别 delta

---

## 3. 引用防幻觉（CRITICAL）

**AI 生成引用有 ~40% 错误率。绝对禁止凭记忆写 BibTeX。**

### 3.1 黄金法则

```
IF 无法程序化获取引用:
    → 标记 [CITATION NEEDED] 或 \cite{PLACEHOLDER_verify}
    → 明确告知用户
    → 绝不编造看似合理的引用
```

### 3.2 五步验证流程

```
1. SEARCH  → Semantic Scholar API 搜索关键词
2. VERIFY  → 至少 2 个来源确认论文存在（S2 + arXiv/CrossRef）
3. RETRIEVE → 通过 DOI 获取 BibTeX（程序化，非记忆）
4. CHECK   → 确认你引用的 claim 确实出自该论文
5. ADD     → 加入 .bib 文件
```

### 3.3 API 速查

| API | 用途 | 限制 |
|-----|------|------|
| **Semantic Scholar** | ML/AI 论文搜索 | 1 RPS (免费) |
| **CrossRef** | DOI → BibTeX | 需 mailto 头 |
| **arXiv** | 预印本搜索 | 3s 间隔 |

```python
# DOI → BibTeX（最可靠的方式）
import requests
def doi_to_bibtex(doi: str) -> str:
    r = requests.get(f"https://doi.org/{doi}",
                     headers={"Accept": "application/x-bibtex"})
    r.raise_for_status()
    return r.text

# Semantic Scholar 搜索
from semanticscholar import SemanticScholar
sch = SemanticScholar()
results = sch.search_paper("attention mechanism transformers", limit=5)
for p in results:
    print(f"{p.title} | DOI: {p.externalIds.get('DOI', 'N/A')}")
```

### 3.4 引用处理规则

| 情况 | 处理 |
|------|------|
| 找到论文 + DOI + BibTeX | 直接用 |
| 找到论文，无 DOI | 用 arXiv BibTeX |
| 论文存在但无法获取 BibTeX | 标记 placeholder，告知用户 |
| 不确定论文是否存在 | 标记 `[CITATION NEEDED]`，告知用户 |
| "我觉得有篇关于 X 的论文" | **绝不引用** — 先搜索或标记 |

---

## 4. 顶会模板速查

### 4.1 ML/AI 会议

| 会议 | 页数限制 | 主文件 | 样式文件 | 必须项 |
|------|---------|--------|---------|--------|
| **NeurIPS** | 9 页 | `main.tex` | `neurips.sty` | Paper Checklist |
| **ICML** | 8 页 (+1 camera-ready) | `example_paper.tex` | `icml2026.sty` | Broader Impact |
| **ICLR** | 9 页 (+1) | `iclr_conference.tex` | `iclr_conference.sty` | LLM 使用声明 |
| **ACL/EMNLP** | 8 页 (long) | `acl_latex.tex` | `acl.sty` | Limitations 必须 |
| **AAAI** | 7 页 (+1) | `aaai_template.tex` | `aaai.sty` | 严格样式 |
| **COLM** | 9 页 (+1) | `colm_conference.tex` | `colm_conference.sty` | 语言模型聚焦 |

### 4.2 系统会议

| 会议 | 页数限制 | 模板类型 | 关键要求 |
|------|---------|---------|---------|
| **OSDI** | 12 页 (+2) | USENIX `usenix.sty` | Research / Operational 双 track |
| **NSDI** | 12 页 | USENIX | Introduction 预筛 |
| **ASPLOS** | 12 页 | ACM `acmart.cls (sigplan)` | 前 2 页快速评审 |
| **SOSP** | 12 页 | ACM `acmart.cls (sigplan)` | 可选 Artifact Evaluation |

### 4.3 模板使用原则

```bash
# 1. 复制整个模板目录（不要只拷 .tex）
cp -r templates/neurips2025/ ~/papers/my-paper/

# 2. 先编译未修改的模板，确认能跑通
latexmk -pdf main.tex

# 3. 逐章替换内容，频繁编译
```

**禁止事项：**
- 不要修改 `.sty` 文件
- 不要在会议模板间复制 `\usepackage` 行
- 不要只复制 `.tex` 而不带 `.sty/.bst`

---

## 5. 写作规范

### 5.1 时间分配（Neel Nanda）

花**大致相等**的时间在：
1. Abstract
2. Introduction
3. 图表
4. **其余所有内容加起来**

审稿人读论文的顺序：标题 → 摘要 → 引言 → 图表 → 也许正文。

### 5.2 Abstract 五句法（Sebastian Farquhar）

```
1. 你做了什么（"We introduce/prove/demonstrate..."）
2. 为什么这很难且重要
3. 怎么做的（含专业关键词以便检索）
4. 有什么证据
5. 最惊人的数字/结果
```

删除一切泛泛的开头：~~"Large language models have achieved remarkable success..."~~

### 5.3 句子级清晰度（Gopen & Swan）

| 原则 | 规则 |
|------|------|
| 主谓紧邻 | 不要在主语和动词之间插入长从句 |
| 重点在句尾 | 把关键数字/结论放在句末 |
| 旧信息在前 | 先放读者已知的内容，再引入新概念 |
| 动词表达动作 | "We analyzed" 而非 "We performed an analysis" |

### 5.4 常见修改

| 问题 | 修复 |
|------|------|
| Abstract 太泛 | 删第一句（如果它能放在任何 ML 论文前面） |
| Introduction 超 1.5 页 | 背景挪到 Related Work |
| 实验没有显式 claim | 每个实验前加 "This tests whether..." |
| 缺统计显著性 | 加 error bars + 运行次数 + 计算方法 |

---

## 6. 投稿工程链

### 6.1 构建

```bash
# 推荐：latexmk 一键构建
latexmk -pdf -interaction=nonstopmode -halt-on-error main.tex

# 手动：需要多次编译
pdflatex main.tex && bibtex main && pdflatex main.tex && pdflatex main.tex
```

### 6.2 Lint + 格式化

```bash
# Lint: 检查常见 LaTeX 问题
chktex main.tex

# 格式化: 减少 diff 噪声
latexindent -w main.tex
```

### 6.3 图表格式

| 类型 | 格式 | 说明 |
|------|------|------|
| 矢量图（plot、diagram） | PDF | matplotlib: `plt.savefig('fig.pdf')` |
| 照片/heatmap | PNG 600dpi 或 TIFF | 栅格图 |
| 表格 | `booktabs` 包 | `\toprule/\midrule/\bottomrule` |

```latex
\usepackage{booktabs}
\begin{tabular}{lcc}
\toprule
Method & Accuracy $\uparrow$ & Latency $\downarrow$ \\
\midrule
Baseline & 85.2 & 45ms \\
\textbf{Ours} & \textbf{92.1} & 38ms \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
```

**图表规范：**
- 用色盲友好色板（Okabe-Ito 或 Paul Tol）
- 图内不放标题（用 caption）
- Caption 独立可理解（不依赖正文）
- 最佳值加粗，标注方向符号（↑ 越高越好，↓ 越低越好）

### 6.4 投稿打包

```bash
# 清理辅助文件
latexmk -c

# 打包投稿
zip -r submission.zip main.tex *.sty *.bst *.bib figures/ --exclude='*.aux' --exclude='*.log'
```

### 6.5 常见失败点

| 问题 | 解决 |
|------|------|
| 图片格式混用导致编译失败 | 统一用 PDF |
| 字体未嵌入 | `pdffonts output.pdf` 检查 |
| Overfull box 过多 | 关键位置手动调行 |
| 引用缺字段 | 检查 DOI/年份/期刊名 |
| 超页数 | 用 `\vspace{-Xpt}` 微调，或精简内容 |

\paragraph{Training Data.}
We sample a 132M-token subset of FineWeb~\citep{penedo2024fineweb} as the real-data source.
To simulate web-scale synthetic contamination, we generate continuations with Qwen3-0.6B~\citep{yang2025qwen3}---the same model we continue pretraining---and inject them at ratio $\rho = 0.4$ via uniform random mixing.
This self-contamination design---where the model's own outputs are mixed back into its training data---creates a particularly challenging detection scenario, as generator and trainee share identical pretrained weights.

\paragraph{Detector.}
We train a TF-IDF + Logistic Regression classifier on a held-out labeled split, achieving AUC\,=\,0.939 with calibrated ECE\,=\,0.048 after temperature scaling ($T = 0.204$).
The resulting $q$-scores have mean 0.60, standard deviation 0.37, and median 0.71, with 46.3\% of samples in the uncertain range $[0.2, 0.8]$.
We use this lightweight detector rather than neural alternatives (e.g., ModernBERT at AUC\,${\geq}$\,0.98 in \citealt{drayson2025detection}) to test whether score \emph{calibration} matters more than raw discrimination for reweighting.

\paragraph{Training.}
We continue pretraining Qwen3-0.6B for 6{,}103 steps (batch size 4, gradient accumulation 4, effective batch 16) with AdamW, cosine schedule (peak lr\,=\,$5{\times}10^{-5}$), max sequence length 2048, and bf16 precision.
The pretrained checkpoint starts at PPL\,=\,22.97 on our held-out set; after continued pretraining, the best method (adaptive $\bstar$) reaches 17.65 ($\Delta$PPL\,=\,$-5.32$, $-23.2\%$).
All main comparisons use three random seeds (42, 123, 456).
We note that method-level differences (${\sim}0.04$ PPL between adaptive and uniform) are small in absolute terms but arise in a regime where the model is already well-optimized; the $5{+}$ PPL drop from pretraining absorbs the easy gains, making further improvement from data curation increasingly difficult.

\paragraph{Evaluation.}
We report held-out perplexity (PPL) on a balanced real/synthetic test set via sliding-window evaluation (stride 1024, 4.08M tokens).
All evaluations are post-hoc with a unified pipeline; training involves no inline evaluation.

\paragraph{Methods.}
We compare five approaches:
\begin{itemize}[nosep,leftmargin=*]
  \item \textbf{Uniform}: $w_j = 1$ for all $j$ (no contamination handling).
  \item \textbf{Grid-$b$}: fixed $b \in \{0.5, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0, 3.0, 5.0\}$, best selected post-hoc by held-out PPL.
        Represents validation-based selection~\citep{drayson2025detection}.
  \item \textbf{ESS-only}: $b^* = \max\{b : \mathrm{ESS}(b) \geq n_{\min}\}$, the maximum-intervention variant retaining only the stability constraint, ablating $\alpha_{\mathrm{eff}}$.
  \item \textbf{Golden Ratio}: $w = 1/\varphi \approx 0.618$ for synthetic ($q_j > 0.5$), $w = 1$ otherwise~\citep{he2025golden}.
        Requires known provenance labels (oracle).
  \item \textbf{Adaptive} (ours): per-batch $b^*$ from the dual-constraint formulation (\S\ref{sec:method}), with $\tau = 0.8$ and $n_{\min} = 2$ (half the micro-batch size).
\end{itemize}

1	\paragraph{Synthetic Contamination and Model Collapse.}
2	Training on recursively generated data leads to irreversible quality degradation---\emph{model collapse}~\citep{shumailov2024model}.
3	\citet{alemohammad2024mad} formalize this as Model Autophagy Disorder, showing that quality or diversity inevitably degrades without fresh real data, even when original training data is retained.
4	More critically, \citet{dohmatob2025strong} prove under scaling-law regimes that even a vanishingly small synthetic fraction (e.g., $1/1000$) suffices to trigger collapse, ruling out data scaling as a remedy.
5	Independent estimates suggest that synthetic content now constitutes 20--60\% of web corpora, making this threat increasingly urgent.
6	These results motivate \emph{contamination-aware} training strategies that explicitly account for synthetic provenance rather than treating all tokens equally.
7	
8	\paragraph{Detection and Filtering of Machine-Generated Text.}
9	Given the severity of contamination, a natural response is to detect and remove synthetic content.
10	DetectGPT~\citep{mitchell2023detectgpt} performs zero-shot detection via probability curvature, while Min-$k$\% Prob~\citep{shi2024minkprob} uses the average log-probability of the lowest-$k$\% tokens as a reference-free signal.
11	Both produce continuous confidence scores suitable as input to reweighting frameworks such as ours.
12	On the mitigation side, \citet{feng2025beyond} prove that even an imperfect verifier prevents collapse, but apply hard binary filtering that discards borderline samples.
13	\citet{guo2025escaping} similarly rely on verification-based selection.
14	Hard filtering requires a precision--recall threshold; soft reweighting avoids this trade-off by assigning continuous weights.
15	
16	Most directly related to our work, \citet{drayson2025detection} propose $w_j = (1{-}q_j)^b$ for collapse prevention via detect-and-reweight, where $q_j$ is the detector's synthetic probability.
17	We adopt the same weighting formula but differ in several fundamental ways.
18	\textbf{(i)}~Drayson et al.\ select $b$ via validation-set grid search and fix it throughout training; different model scales require different values ($b{=}10$ for ${\leq}360$M, $b{=}1$ for 1.7B), making the choice \emph{per-model} and expensive.
19	Our $b^*$ is derived per-batch from dual constraints ($\alpha_{\mathrm{eff}} \geq \tau$, $\mathrm{ESS} \geq n_{\min}$) at zero validation cost, following a \emph{minimum intervention} principle that selects the smallest exponent satisfying the quality floor.
20	\textbf{(ii)}~Their SIR resampling discretizes the weight distribution; we apply direct loss reweighting with continuous gradients.
21	\textbf{(iii)}~They employ a ModernBERT-150M detector (AUC\,=\,0.986) on WikiText-2 (${\sim}$2M tokens); we show that a lightweight TF-IDF+LR detector (AUC\,=\,0.939) suffices on FineWeb-scale data (132M+ tokens), suggesting that score calibration matters more than raw detection accuracy.
22	
23	\paragraph{Data Mixing and Instance-Level Reweighting.}
24	A parallel line of work optimizes data composition without targeting synthetic contamination.
25	At the \emph{domain} level, DoReMi~\citep{xie2023doremi} learns mixture weights via Group DRO with a proxy model, DSIR~\citep{xie2023dsir} performs importance resampling with $n$-gram features, and \citet{ye2025mixing} discover predictable functional forms relating mixing ratios to performance.
26	AIOLI~\citep{chen2025aioli} unifies these into an online adaptive framework, while \citet{yang2026mixing} train an RL agent for domain-weight selection.
27	These methods do not address instance-level contamination within a domain.
28	At the \emph{instance} level, SoftDedup~\citep{he2024softdedup} downweights high-frequency samples via $n$-gram commonness, \citet{sow2025dynamic} derive sample weights from per-sample loss with convergence guarantees, and \citet{kuo2024weighting} show that differentiated weighting of LLM-generated data improves downstream classification.
29	Our reweighting differs from all of these in being driven by \emph{provenance}---detector scores estimating human vs.\ synthetic origin---rather than loss, frequency, or domain membership.
30	
31	\paragraph{Theoretical Foundations.}
32	\citet{he2025golden} derive the optimal real-data weight under known mixture proportions, finding the golden-ratio reciprocal (${\approx}0.62$) optimal when both sources are equally sized.
33	Their result requires the contamination ratio $k$, unavailable in web-scale settings; we use it as an oracle baseline.
34	\citet{wang2026survive} prove that contaminated recursive training converges at a rate governed by the effective real-data fraction $\alpha$, providing the theoretical motivation for our quality threshold: ensuring $\alpha_{\mathrm{eff}}(b) \geq \tau$ guarantees a convergence-rate lower bound.
35	We operationalize this without the known-proportion assumption, estimating $\alpha_{\mathrm{eff}}$ from batch-level statistics online.
36	For the stability constraint, we build on Kish's effective sample size and the Pareto-smoothed importance sampling framework of \citet{vehtari2024psis}.
37	\citet{kimura2024iw} provide a broader treatment of importance weighting under distribution shift, within which our provenance-based reweighting can be viewed as a special case of covariate-shift correction where the covariate is synthetic origin probability.
38	
39	\smallskip
40	\noindent\textbf{Summary.}
41	No existing method provides principled per-batch exponent selection without validation.
42	Our dual-constraint framework fills this gap by deriving the \emph{minimum intervention} $b^*$ from batch-level diagnostics alone, eliminating the per-model grid search of prior work while retaining theoretical grounding in convergence analysis and importance sampling.

\textbf{(ii)}~Their SIR resampling discretizes the weight distribution; we apply direct loss reweighting with continuous gradients.

\paragraph{Data Mixing and Instance-Level Reweighting.}
A parallel line of work optimizes data composition without targeting synthetic contamination.
At the \emph{domain} level, DoReMi~\citep{xie2023doremi} learns mixture weights via Group DRO with a proxy model, DSIR~\citep{xie2023dsir} performs importance resampling with $n$-gram features, and \citet{ye2025mixing} discover predictable functional forms relating mixing ratios to performance.

At the \emph{instance} level, SoftDedup~\citep{he2024softdedup} downweights high-frequency samples via $n$-gram commonness, \citet{sow2025dynamic} derive sample weights from per-sample loss with convergence guarantees, and \citet{kuo2024weighting} show that differentiated weighting of LLM-generated data improves downstream classification.

No existing method provides principled per-batch exponent selection without validation.

Web pretraining corpora are increasingly contaminated by machine-generated text, with recent estimates placing the synthetic fraction between 20\% and 60\%.
This poses a fundamental threat to model quality: \citet{shumailov2024model} demonstrate that training on recursively generated data leads to irreversible model collapse, and \citet{dohmatob2025strong} prove under scaling-law regimes that even a vanishingly small synthetic fraction suffices to trigger degradation, ruling out data scaling as a remedy.
As synthetic content becomes ubiquitous, \emph{contamination-aware training}---strategies that explicitly account for data provenance during optimization---is necessary for maintaining pretraining quality.

A natural mitigation is detect-and-reweight: assign each sample a weight $w(x) = (1 - q(x))^b$ based on a detector's estimated synthetic probability $q(x)$, where larger $b$ downweights suspected synthetic text more aggressively \citep{drayson2025detection}.
However, the exponent $b$ is a sensitive per-model hyperparameter whose optimal value varies by an order of magnitude across scales: $b = 1$ for SmolLM-1.7B versus $b = 10$ for GPT-2 124M.
Selecting $b$ requires a clean validation set and grid search costing up to $6{\times}$ the base training budget.
The practical question is immediate: \emph{how should $b$ be chosen without validation data?}

We propose a \emph{dual-constraint framework} that derives the exponent adaptively per batch from two diagnostics computed on the detector scores alone.
The effective real proportion $\aeff(b)$ measures the weighted fraction of gradient signal attributable to real data and imposes a \emph{quality floor}: $\aeff(b) \geq \tau$---at least enough cleaning.
Kish's effective sample size $\mathrm{ESS}(b)$ \citep{vehtari2024psis} quantifies weight concentration and imposes a \emph{stability ceiling}: $\mathrm{ESS}(b) \geq \nmin$---not so much cleaning that gradient signal degrades.
A key structural insight makes the framework tractable: $\aeff$ is monotonically non-decreasing in $b$ while $\mathrm{ESS}$ is monotonically non-increasing, so the quality constraint yields a lower bound $\btau$ and the stability constraint an upper bound $\bess$.
We adopt a \emph{minimum intervention principle}:
\begin{equation*}
  \bstar = \inf\{b \geq 0 : \aeff(b) \geq \tau\} \quad \text{subject to} \quad \mathrm{ESS}(\bstar) \geq \nmin,
\end{equation*}
the smallest exponent satisfying the quality floor.
This is deliberately conservative: apply enough decontamination to meet the quality target, but no more, thereby preserving the largest possible effective sample size.
In practice, batches fall into three regimes---already clean ($\bstar = 0$), quality-binding ($\bstar = \btau$), and stability-binding ($\bstar = \bess$)---allowing the framework to handle heterogeneous contamination levels naturally.
Unlike the discrete sampling-importance-resampling of \citet{drayson2025detection}, we implement $\bstar$ through direct loss reweighting with continuous gradient scaling.

We evaluate on continued pretraining of Qwen3-0.6B on 132M FineWeb tokens with 40\% self-generated synthetic contamination (\S\ref{sec:experiments}).
Adaptive $\bstar$ with default hyperparameters ($\tau = 0.8$, $\nmin = 2$) matches the grid-search-optimal fixed $b$ within seed variance (PPL 17.65 vs.\ 17.65, capturing 88.6\% of the grid-best improvement over uniform), while eliminating the grid search cost.
It outperforms both uniform training (PPL 17.69) and ESS-only maximum intervention (PPL 17.73), confirming that minimum intervention is the better operating point.
A lightweight TF-IDF + logistic regression detector (AUC\,=\,0.939) suffices, with score calibration mattering more than raw detection accuracy.
The quality threshold $\tau$ admits a safe operating range of $[0.5, 0.8]$, with all tested values improving over uniform training.

Our contributions are:
\begin{enumerate}[nosep,leftmargin=*]
  \item A dual-constraint framework for adaptive $\bstar$ selection with minimum intervention semantics, providing validation-free per-batch exponent derivation from batch-level diagnostics (\S\ref{sec:method}).
  \item Empirical evidence that adaptive $\bstar$ matches grid-search-optimal performance within seed variance at zero validation cost, and that minimum intervention outperforms maximum intervention (\S\ref{sec:results}).
  \item A demonstration that a lightweight TF-IDF + logistic regression detector suffices for effective reweighting, with score calibration mattering more than raw detection accuracy (\S\ref{sec:experiments}--\ref{sec:results}).
\end{enumerate}
